title: Decision: a link-joined call is its own call, with its own secret, authenticating nobody
description:
Mark decided 2026-11-23, for bead mimid-1wgh.114.7 (mimid terminating
calls in an SFU of its own).

THE QUESTION. Mark's reason for an SFU is to give the front ends with no
media stack something to call: an IRC user clicks a link and talks. But
a person who followed a link IS NOT A MEMBER OF THE MLS GROUP, and the
media key is derived from an epoch of that group
(draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.3). A browser that followed a URL is not in
it and can derive nothing. So what is a link-joined call?

OPTIONS WEIGHED:
(a) The SFU holds a key for link-joined participants and relays or mixes
    for them. One call, everyone hears each other, NOT end-to-end
    encrypted against the provider.
(b) A link-joined call is a SEPARATE call with its own minted secret,
    encrypted among whoever holds the link, authenticating nobody.
(c) The SFU forwards only and link-joined participants get nothing: one
    kind of call, properly keyed, IRC left where it is.

CHOSEN: (b).

WHY:
- Nothing then claims to be what it is not. An MLS-keyed call is
  confined to the room's members and says so; a link call is confined to
  whoever holds the link and says that. Two honest statements beat one
  statement that is true for some participants and false for others.
- (a)'s cost is the worse kind: it is one call whose security property
  differs per participant, which no interface can explain. A client
  cannot show a lock for the MLS members and no lock for the browser
  guests in the same call, and AGENTS.md forbids describing mimid as
  protecting against a malicious provider, which (a) would make
  routinely necessary to qualify.
- (c) is defensible and was the fallback, but it leaves Mark's reason
  for the SFU unserved: IRC would still be clicking links to other
  people's services.
- (b) is ParlorVTC's model exactly -- ephemeral keys, anonymous
  visitors, encryption among whoever has the link -- so there is a
  working design to copy rather than invent, and Parlor's own SPEC is
  straight about what it does not give you ("Supplicants are anonymous
  by design").

WHAT IT MEANS TO BUILD:
- Two call kinds, named differently to the user wherever either is
  shown. A link call is not "a call that is less encrypted"; it is a
  different thing, and the words for it must not borrow the other's.
- The link secret is MINTED, not derived: random, fragment-only in the
  URL so it never reaches a server, and rotated per call. It
  authenticates nobody, so a link call cannot tell its participants
  apart and must not pretend to -- no participant list that implies
  identity.
- The SFU forwards encrypted frames for the MLS call
  (jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §2: "the SFU sees encrypted frames and
  forwards them by SSRC") and holds the link call's secret, because the
  link call's participants cannot agree one among themselves.
- Which means the SFU DOES see link-call media if it mixes. If it only
  forwards, it does not. That is a further decision when the SFU is
  built, not now.

NOT DECIDED HERE: whether to build the SFU at all. This decides what a
link-joined call IS if one is built, so that the question does not get
answered by accident during the work.
close_reason: Mark 2026-11-23: a link-joined call is its own call with its own minted secret, authenticating nobody; two kinds of call named differently.
